Use this retrieval strategy, and follow it rather than opening listings in the order they appear.
1. Read the advertised price of every listing above first. That price is the cheapest option in that listing that can be bought, so nothing in it that can be bought costs less.
2. Open listings in ascending order of advertised price. For each one, do two separate things. First, choose the option asked about, then look at the page again and read the price it now shows. The price a listing shows before you choose is its cheapest option that can be bought, not necessarily the one asked about, and the reply to choosing an option does not show the new price. Second, check whether that option can actually be bought. An option can be listed and still be unavailable, in which case it is shown as disabled or greyed out and cannot be chosen from the menu, so it has no price you can use.
3. A listing only becomes your best candidate if the option is both cheaper and available. A cheaper unavailable one changes nothing.
4. Skip every unopened listing whose advertised price is at or above your best available total. Such a listing cannot win whatever its stock.
5. Stop when no unopened listing has an advertised price below your best available total.
In your answer, name the seller, give the price, and say explicitly that you checked the option was available rather than only listed. Say how many listings you opened, how many you skipped, and how many you rejected for being unavailable.
Important: the figure this bound produces is a limit used only to decide what to skip. It is not a price read for the option asked about, and must never appear in your answer as one. Only report a price you read from a listing you opened, for the exact option asked about, read after that option was chosen. Never pair an advertised price with an option unless you saw that price shown while that option was chosen.

result.final: The least you'd have to pay for a medium Larchmere tee that's actually in stock is $19.17, from Elmsworth Apparel (http://localhost:7770/igr-dev-34.html). I explicitly checked availability rather than just seeing it listed: Elmsworth's Medium size option was enabled/selectable in the Size menu (not disabled or greyed out), and after choosing Medium the product page displayed $19.17 for that exact option. Budget check: opened 8 listings in ascending advertised-price order (Brindle $14.18, Lymington $15.18, Dunmore $16.45, Bexhill $16.75, Elmsworth $17.83, Haldane $17.97, Northwick $18.16, Everleigh $19.05); skipped 13 listings whose advertised price was at or above the best available total of $19.17 (Pentland $23.78 through Dovercourt $41.55); and rejected 5 listings for unavailable Medium stock (Brindle and Dunmore offered no Medium option at all; Lymington, Haldane, and Northwick showed Medium disabled). Among available Mediums, Bexhill read $21.71 and Everleigh $21.54 after selection; Elmsworth's $19.17 was the cheapest available.
